files.feature.md: A broker delivers tenant billing commands at least once. Producers authenticate, but message identity, duplicate handling, ordering, retry limits, dead-letter access and idempotency scope are undecided. One authorized command must still succeed.

prompt: Use $security-threat-model to model this document lifecycle. Ask only material questions before the final model.

files.design.md: Private tenant documents are written to a primary database, indexed for search, cached for previews, exported by background jobs and included in backups. Users may revoke sharing and delete documents. Operators can restore backups, but the design does not state how current ACLs, deletion tombstones or tenant identity are reapplied.

prompt: Use $security-implementation to propose SDK-independent pseudocode and tests for the requested account-linking and recovery flow.

files.contract.md: A signed-in user may link an external identity after fresh authentication. The callback must belong to the initiating session and intended provider. Recovery codes are one-time and expire. Linking or recovery invalidates earlier pending attempts and product-policy sessions. Do not choose an SDK or invent browser APIs.
